sort_order.x-autobe-specification: Sorting direction parameter. Used in ORDER BY clause as ASC or DESC. Valid values: asc, desc. Defaults to desc (newest/highest first) if not specified.

IEcommerceMallSalesAnalytic.IRequest.description:
Request body for querying sales analytics data with comprehensive filtering and pagination capabilities.

This request enables sellers and administrators to retrieve aggregated sales statistics across various dimensions including date ranges, order statuses, sellers, and product categories. The operation calculates key metrics such as total revenue, order counts, and average order values from the order and order item tables.

Date range filtering is enforced with a maximum 90-day window to maintain query performance. All filter parameters are optional, allowing flexible querying from broad overviews to highly specific analyses. Pagination supports offset-based navigation for large result sets.

Sorting can be applied on creation date, total price, or status fields with ascending or descending order. The response includes aggregated sales summaries optimized for dashboard displays and reporting interfaces.
IEcommerceMallSalesAnalytic.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Query parameters for filtering and paginating sales analytics data. Parameters are used to construct WHERE clauses and ORDER BY clauses when querying ecommerce_mall_orders and ecommerce_mall_order_items tables. Date range filtering (date_from, date_to) constrains order.created_at. Status filtering applies to order.status. seller_id and category_id filter by foreign key relationships. search performs text matching on order_number and product names. page and limit control offset-based pagination. sort_by and sort_order control result ordering. All filters are optional and combined with AND logic.

id.description: Unique identifier for the refund request record.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests.id. UUID format primary key.

reason.description: Customer-provided reason for requesting the refund.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests.reason. Customer-provided text explaining refund request.

status.description: Current status of the refund request workflow.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests.status. Values: pending (awaiting seller response), approved (seller approved refund), rejected (seller denied refund).

requested_at.description: Timestamp when the customer submitted the refund request.
requested_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests.requested_at. DateTime with timezone (timestamptz).

responded_at.description: Timestamp when the seller responded to the refund request (approved or rejected). Null while request is pending.
responded_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests.responded_at. Nullable DateTime; null while request status is pending, populated when seller approves or rejects.

days_since_delivery.description: Number of days elapsed since the order item was delivered. Used to validate 7-day refund window.
days_since_delivery.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests.days_since_delivery. Integer value used to enforce 7-day refund window eligibility.

order_number.description: Order number of the parent order containing the order item for which this refund was requested.
order_number.x-autobe-specification: Computed via JOIN: ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests -> ecommerce_mall_order_items -> ecommerce_mall_orders. Retrieves orders.order_number from the parent order associated with this refund request's order item.

product_name.description: Name of the product associated with the order item for which this refund was requested.
product_name.x-autobe-specification: Computed via JOIN chain: ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests -> ecommerce_mall_order_items -> ecommerce_mall_product_variants -> ecommerce_mall_products. Retrieves products.name from the product associated with this refund request's order item variant.

seller_shop_name.description: Shop name of the seller who owns the product associated with this refund request.
seller_shop_name.x-autobe-specification: Computed via JOIN chain: ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests -> ecommerce_mall_order_items -> ecommerce_mall_product_variants -> ecommerce_mall_products -> ecommerce_mall_sellers. Retrieves sellers.shop_name from the seller who owns the product associated with this refund request's order item variant.

created_at.description: Record creation timestamp for audit purposes.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests.created_at. DateTime with timezone (timestamptz). System-generated on record creation.

updated_at.description: Record last update timestamp for tracking modifications.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests.updated_at. DateTime with timezone (timestamptz). Updated on status changes or modifications.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if the record is active, populated when soft-deleted for archival.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests.deleted_at. Nullable DateTime; null for active records, populated when soft-deleted for archival purposes.

IEcommerceMallOrderItemRefundRequest.ISu.description: Lightweight refund request summary for paginated listing views in seller and admin dashboards. Contains essential information including refund reason, current status, submission timestamp, days since delivery for 7-day window validation, and contextual data from related order, product, and seller entities. Used for reviewing pending refund requests without loading full request details.
IEcommerceMallOrderItemRefundRequest.ISu.x-autobe-specification: Direct column mapping for id, reason, status, requested_at, responded_at, days_since_delivery, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at from ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests. Computed properties via JOIN chains: order_number from orders table via order_items, product_name from products table via order_items and product_variants, seller_shop_name from sellers table via order_items, product_variants, and products. Responded_at is nullable (null while request pending). Deleted_at is nullable for soft-deletion support.

priceRange.description: Price range across variants if different from base price

productCount.description: Number of products in this category

oneOf.description: Seller approval status
Seller approval status
Seller approval status

productCount.description: Number of products sold by this seller

IEcommerceMallSearchResult.ISummary.description: Unified search result representing a matched entity from products, categories, or sellers. Used in paginated search responses to display search results with appropriate entity-specific information. Each result includes a type discriminator to enable client-side rendering of different entity types.
IEcommerceMallSearchResult.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Unified search result computed from three sources: ecommerce_mall_products (JOIN with sellers, categories, images, reviews), ecommerce_mall_categories, ecommerce_mall_sellers. Each result includes type discriminator: 'product', 'category', or 'seller'. Product results: JOIN products with seller (shop_name), category (name), first image (thumbnail), calculate avg rating from reviews. Category results: direct from categories table. Seller results: direct from sellers table with approval_status. All results include relevance_score from trigram matching.

IEcommerceMallProductReviewSummary.description: Review summary statistics for a product. Provides aggregated data including the average customer rating (rounded to 1 decimal place), total number of non-deleted reviews, and a breakdown of ratings by star level (1-5 stars). This information helps customers assess product quality before purchasing. All statistics are calculated from non-deleted reviews only.

average_rating.description: Average customer rating rounded to one decimal place, calculated from all non-deleted reviews for this product. Null when the product has no reviews or all reviews are deleted.
average_rating.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: ROUND(AVG(rating), 1) from ecommerce_mall_reviews WHERE product_id = {path parameter} AND is_deleted = false. Returns null if COUNT = 0 (no reviews or all deleted). Range: 1.0 to 5.0 when not null.

review_count.description: Total count of non-deleted reviews for this product. Excludes reviews where is_deleted is true.
review_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT(*) from ecommerce_mall_reviews WHERE product_id = {path parameter} AND is_deleted = false. Returns 0 if no non-deleted reviews exist.

rating_distribution.description: Breakdown of review counts by star rating level. Object with five keys (1 through 5), where each key's value represents the count of reviews with that specific star rating. All keys are always present, even if count is zero.
rating_distribution.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: GROUP BY rating with COUNT(*) from ecommerce_mall_reviews WHERE product_id = {path parameter} AND is_deleted = false. Returns object with keys 1-5, each containing the count of reviews with that rating. All five keys (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) are always present with integer values >= 0.

IEcommerceMallProductReviewSummary.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation schema for product review statistics. Query ecommerce_mall_reviews table WHERE product_id = {path parameter} AND is_deleted = false. Calculate: (1) average_rating = ROUND(AVG(rating), 1) as number or null if no reviews, (2) review_count = COUNT(*) as integer, (3) rating_distribution = GROUP BY rating with COUNT for each value 1-5. Use index on [product_id, created_at] for efficient filtering. Return 404 if product_id invalid. This schema does not map to a single database table but represents computed aggregations from the reviews table.

status.description: Filter by cancellation request status: pending, approved, or rejected
status.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for filtering by cancellation request status. Maps to ecommerce_mall_order_item_cancellation_requests.status column for WHERE clause filtering: status = 'pending' (awaiting seller response), status = 'approved' (seller approved, item cancelled), or status = 'rejected' (seller rejected, item continues processing). Not a direct entity field but a filter criterion.

requested_at_from.description: Filter cancellation requests submitted from this timestamp
requested_at_from.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for filtering cancellation requests by submission date range. Maps to ecommerce_mall_order_item_cancellation_requests.requested_at column for WHERE clause: requested_at >= requested_at_from (inclusive). Filters requests submitted from this timestamp. Format: ISO 8601 date-time string. Not a direct entity field but a filter criterion.

requested_at_to.description: Filter cancellation requests submitted until this timestamp
requested_at_to.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for filtering cancellation requests by submission date range. Maps to ecommerce_mall_order_item_cancellation_requests.requested_at column for WHERE clause: requested_at <= requested_at_to (inclusive). Filters requests submitted until this timestamp. Format: ISO 8601 date-time string. Not a direct entity field but a filter criterion.

responded_at_from.description: Filter cancellation requests responded from this timestamp
responded_at_from.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for filtering cancellation requests by response date range. Maps to ecommerce_mall_order_item_cancellation_requests.responded_at column for WHERE clause: responded_at >= responded_at_from (inclusive). Filters requests where seller responded from this timestamp. Nullable column - only matches records where seller has responded. Format: ISO 8601 date-time string. Not a direct entity field but a filter criterion.

responded_at_to.description: Filter cancellation requests responded until this timestamp
responded_at_to.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for filtering cancellation requests by response date range. Maps to ecommerce_mall_order_item_cancellation_requests.responded_at column for WHERE clause: responded_at <= responded_at_to (inclusive). Filters requests where seller responded until this timestamp. Nullable column - only matches records where seller has responded. Format: ISO 8601 date-time string. Not a direct entity field but a filter criterion.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based)
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination control parameter for list queries. Controls which page of results to return (1-based indexing). Combined with limit to calculate offset for offset-based pagination or used for cursor positioning. Minimum value: 1. Not mapped to any database column - purely a query parameter. Used by Realize/Test agents to implement pagination logic in list queries.

limit.description: Number of items per page (max 100)
limit.x-autobe-specification: Pagination control parameter for list queries. Defines maximum number of records per page. Minimum value: 1, maximum value: 100. Enforced by API validation to prevent excessive data retrieval. Not mapped to any database column - purely a query parameter. Used by Realize/Test agents to implement pagination logic in list queries. Combined with page to calculate offset for offset-based pagination.

IEcommerceMallOrderItemCancellationReque.description: Request parameters for filtering and paginating order item cancellation request listings. Supports filtering by cancellation request status (pending, approved, rejected) and date ranges for both request submission and seller response timestamps, with pagination controls for efficient data retrieval across customer, seller, and admin endpoints.
IEcommerceMallOrderItemCancellationReque.x-autobe-specification: Filter and pagination parameters for cancellation request list queries. Used across customer, seller, and admin endpoints to filter by status and date ranges, with pagination controls. Filtering fields map to ecommerce_mall_order_item_cancellation_requests columns for WHERE clause: status (exact match on status column), requested_at_from/to (range filtering on requested_at column), responded_at_from/to (range filtering on responded_at column). Pagination fields (page, limit) control result set size. All fields optional. Supports cursor-based or offset pagination on the cancellation requests table.

reason.description: Violation reason provided by the administrator for audit trail purposes. Documents why the product is being force-deleted due to policy violations.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Computed field - violation reason provided by administrator for audit trail. Recorded in system audit logs and product snapshots. No direct database column mapping - used to document why force-deletion was performed.

IEcommerceMallProduct.IForceDelete.description: Request body for administrator force-delete operation. Contains violation reason for audit trail when removing products due to policy violations. This DTO is used exclusively by administrators to enforce platform policies by removing products that violate terms, regardless of order status or seller ownership.
IEcommerceMallProduct.IForceDelete.x-autobe-specification: Request body for administrator force-delete operation. Does not map to database storage directly - triggers product deletion with status='deleted' and deleted_at timestamp update. The reason field is recorded in system audit logs and product snapshots. Excluded all database columns (id, name, description, base_price, status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, seller_id, category_id) as they are either path parameters, auto-managed, or not changeable in force-delete. Excluded all relations (seller, category, variants, images, productSnapshots, reviews, wishlistEntries) as this is a request DTO, not a response DTO.

id.description: Unique identifier of the order item captured at snapshot time.
id.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's order_item_id field. UUID string representing the order item identifier.

quantity.description: Quantity of the product variant purchased in this order item.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's quantity field. Integer value from order_items.quantity column.

unitPrice.description: Unit price at time of purchase. Immutable after order creation.
unitPrice.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's unitPrice field. Decimal value from order_items.unit_price column at purchase time.

status.description: Order item fulfillment status: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded.
status.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's status field. String value from order_items.status column representing fulfillment state.

productName.description: Product name captured at snapshot time.
productName.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's productName field. String value from products.name column at snapshot time.

productDescription.description: Product description captured at snapshot time.
productDescription.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's productDescription field. Text value from products.description column at snapshot time.

variantSku.description: SKU code of the product variant captured at snapshot time.
variantSku.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's variantSku field. String value from product_variants.sku_code column.

variantOptions.description: Option values defining the variant configuration (e.g., {"color": "red", "size": "large"}).
variantOptions.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's variantOptions field. JSON object containing key-value pairs from product_variant_options representing variant configuration.

sellerShopName.description: Seller shop name captured at snapshot time.
sellerShopName.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's sellerShopName field. String value from sellers.shop_name column at snapshot time.

sellerLogo.description: Seller logo URL captured at snapshot time. Null if no logo uploaded.
sellerLogo.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's sellerLogo field. Nullable string value from sellers.logo_url column. Null if seller has no logo uploaded.

createdAt.description: Order item creation timestamp (ISO 8601 date-time with timezone).
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's createdAt field. DateTime value from order_items.created_at column in ISO 8601 format with timezone.

updatedAt.description: Order item last update timestamp (ISO 8601 date-time with timezone).
updatedAt.x-autobe-specification: Extracted from JSON snapshot's updatedAt field. DateTime value from order_items.updated_at column in ISO 8601 format with timezone.

IEcommerceMallOrderItemSnapshot.IValue.description: Complete order item state snapshot value capturing all product, variant, pricing, status, and seller information extracted from JSON snapshot data at the time of a lifecycle event. Used for audit trail verification and dispute resolution on the e-commerce platform, preserving historical state even after source entities are modified.
IEcommerceMallOrderItemSnapshot.IValue.x-autobe-specification: Computed JSON snapshot value type extracted from ecommerce_mall_order_item_snapshots.current_values or previous_values JSON columns. All fields are parsed from the JSON snapshot stored in the database, representing the complete order item state at a specific lifecycle event. Fields are extracted via JSON parsing: id (order_item_id UUID), quantity (integer from order_items), unitPrice (decimal from order_items.unit_price), status (string from order_items.status), productName (string from products.name), productDescription (text from products.description), variantSku (string from product_variants.sku_code), variantOptions (JSON object from product_variant_options), sellerShopName (string from sellers.shop_name), sellerLogo (nullable string from sellers.logo_url), createdAt (datetime from order_items.created_at), updatedAt (datetime from order_items.updated_at). The snapshot captures product, variant, pricing, status, and seller profile information as it existed at the snapshot time for audit trail and dispute resolution purposes.

IJsonObject.description:
Generic JSON object type for storing flexible key-value data structures.

Used in audit trail snapshots to capture complete state information at specific points in time. The structure varies depending on the entity type being snapshot (products, order items, reviews, etc.) and can contain any valid JSON values including nested objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null values.

This type provides a flexible container for dynamic data that doesn't have a fixed schema, allowing snapshots to preserve complete entity state regardless of future schema changes.
IJsonObject.x-autobe-specification: Generic JSON object type for storing arbitrary snapshot data. Used in order item snapshots to capture previous and current state as flexible key-value structures. No direct database mapping - represents dynamic JSON content stored in String columns (previous_values, current_values). Downstream agents should parse as JSON objects with arbitrary properties.

key.description: The option attribute name for this variant option, such as 'color', 'size', or 'material'.
key.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options.key column. Stores the option attribute name such as 'color', 'size', or 'material'. Required string field with unique constraint per variant.

value.description: The selected option value corresponding to the option name, such as 'Red', 'Large', or 'Cotton'.
value.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options.value column. Stores the selected option value such as 'Red', 'Large', or 'Cotton'. Required string field.

IEcommerceMallProductVariantOption.description: A key-value pair representing a single product variant option. Used to define variant configurations like color, size, or material. Each product variant must have at least one option value, and options are stored in a normalized table structure to ensure First Normal Form (1NF) compliance for efficient querying and filtering.
IEcommerceMallProductVariantOption.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options table. Each row represents one option attribute for a product variant. The key column stores the option name (e.g., 'color', 'size', 'material'), and the value column stores the selected option value (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton'). Both columns are required strings with a unique constraint on [ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id, key] ensuring each variant has at most one option per attribute name. During variant creation, an array of key-value pairs is transformed into individual INSERT statements for this table. The FK column ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id and variant relation are excluded from this DTO as they are managed at the parent variant level.

text:
I'll now execute the **test** agent to generate comprehensive E2E test suites for all your e-commerce platform API interfaces. This will create tests that validate both individual endpoints and their integrated workflows.

The test agent will cover:
- **Authentication Flows**: Customer/Seller registration, login, password management
- **Profile & Address Tests**: CRUD operations with snapshot validation
- **Product Catalog Tests**: Search, filtering, categories, variants, inventory
- **Shopping Experience Tests**: Wishlist, cart operations
- **Order Lifecycle Tests**: Checkout, payment, order creation, status tracking
- **Shipping Tests**: Shipment creation, tracking, delivery confirmation
- **Cancellation/Refund Tests**: Request workflows, approval/rejection
- **Review Tests**: Create, edit, delete with rating calculations
- **Admin Operations**: User management, seller oversight, product/order control
- **Snapshot Validation**: Verify all snapshots are created correctly

instruction:
# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform E2E Test Requirements

## Authentication Tests

### Customer Authentication
- Test customer registration with valid email and password
- Test customer registration with duplicate email (should fail)
- Test customer login with correct credentials
- Test customer login with incorrect password (should fail)
- Test customer password change with correct current password
- Test customer password change with incorrect current password (should fail)
- Test customer account deletion
- Test customer cannot access protected routes without authentication

### Seller Authentication
- Test seller registration with valid email and password
- Test seller registration with duplicate email (should fail)
- Test seller login with correct credentials
- Test seller login with incorrect password (should fail)
- Test seller password change with correct current password
- Test seller password change with incorrect current password (should fail)
- Test seller approval status is initially "pending"
- Test seller account deletion with validation (no pending orders, no pending cancellation/refund requests)
- Test seller cannot delete account if conditions not met

### Administrator Authentication
- Test administrator login
- Test user request to become administrator
- Test super administrator approve/reject admin requests
- Test administrator grade promotion/demotion

## Customer Profile Tests
- Test view customer profile
- Test edit customer profile (display name, phone number)
- Verify snapshot is created on profile edit
- Test customer profile snapshot can be viewed

## Address Management Tests
- Test create new shipping address
- Test list all customer addresses
- Test edit existing address
- Test delete address
- Test set default shipping address
- Test customer can have multiple addresses with one default

## Category Tests
- Test list all categories (including subcategories)
- Test view category details with products
- Test products within category can be browsed
- (Admin only) Test create category/subcategory
- (Admin only) Test edit category name and description
- (Admin only) Test delete category (products become uncategorized)

## Product Tests

### Product CRUD
- Test create product with all required fields (name, description, category, base price)
- Test view product details (all images, variants, seller info, reviews)
- Test edit product (all fields including images)
- Verify product snapshot is created on edit
- Test product snapshot can be viewed by owner and admin
- Test delete product with validation (no pending order items, no pending cancellation/refund)
- Test deleted product does not appear in search or category listings
- Test deleted product snapshots are preserved

### Product Images
- Test upload multiple images for product
- Test reorder images (first image is thumbnail)
- Test delete images from product
- Verify image changes are included in product snapshots

### Product Variants (SKU)
- Test add variant to product (SKU code, option values, price, stock quantity)
- Test variant SKU code must be unique
- Test edit variant (SKU code, option values, price)
- Verify variant snapshot is created on edit
- Test delete variant with validation (no pending order items, no pending cancellation/refund)
- Test product with no variants is visible but shown as "unavailable"
- Test product must have at least one variant to be purchasable

### Product Search
- Test search products by name
- Test search results are paginated
- Test filter search by category
- Test filter search by price range (min, max)
- Test filter search by in-stock only
- Test sort by newest first
- Test sort by price low-to-high
- Test sort by price high-to-low
- Test search shows products from all sellers

### Product Listing
- Test product listing shows: main image, name, base price/price range, seller shop name, average rating
- Test listing is paginated

## Inventory Management Tests
- Test view inventory history for variant
- Test add inventory (restock with quantity and reason)
- Test subtract inventory (adjustment/loss with quantity and reason)
- Test current stock is calculated by summing all inventory records
- Test variant shows "out of stock" when stock reaches 0
- Test out of stock variant cannot be added to cart
- Test order placement creates negative inventory record
- Test order cancellation/restores stock via positive inventory record
- Test refund restores stock via positive inventory record

## Wishlist Tests
- Test add product to wishlist
- Test view customer wishlist (paginated)
- Test remove product from wishlist
- Test deleted product is automatically removed from all wishlists
- Test wishlist shows products (not specific variants)

## Shopping Cart Tests
- Test add variant to cart with quantity
- Test same variant in cart combines quantities (not separate line)
- Test view cart with: product name, variant options, price, quantity, subtotal, total
- Test update cart item quantity
- Test remove item from cart
- Test stock quantity warning when cart quantity exceeds available stock
- Test deleted variant marked as unavailable in cart
- Test out of stock variant marked as unavailable in cart

## Checkout & Order Tests

### Checkout
- Test proceed to checkout from cart
- Test unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Test select shipping address (or use default)
- Test review order summary (items, prices, address, total)
- Test place order with payment confirmation
- Test payment failure does not create order (customer can retry)
- Test payment success creates order
- Test shipping address cannot be changed after order placed

### Order Management
- Test view customer order history (paginated, newest first)
- Test order list shows: order number, date, total price, overall status
- Test view order details (items, shipping address, shipments)
- Test order status derived from item statuses correctly

### Order Item Status
- Test order item status: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded
- Test each order item has independent status

### Order Status
- Test order status "paid" when all items are paid
- Test order status "shipped" when any item is shipped (none delivered)
- Test order status "delivered" when all items are delivered
- Test order status "cancelled" when all items are cancelled
- Test order status "refunded" when all items are refunded
- Test order status "partially completed" for mixed states

## Shipping & Tracking Tests

### Shipment Management
- Test seller can view order items needing shipping
- Test create shipment (select items, enter tracking info: carrier name, tracking number)
- Test different sellers ship separately (different shipments)
- Test seller can bundle multiple items into one shipment
- Test all items in same shipment share tracking information
- Test items change to "shipped" status when shipment created
- Test view shipment tracking information

### Delivery Confirmation
- Test customer can view shipments for order
- Test customer confirm delivery per shipment
- Test items in confirmed shipment change to "delivered" status
- Test auto-delivery after 14 days from shipping

## Cancellation & Refund Tests

### Cancellation Requests
- Test request cancellation for order item with status "paid"
- Test cannot request cancellation for item with status "shipped" or later
- Test cancellation request includes reason (text)
- Test seller can approve cancellation request
- Test seller can reject cancellation request
- Verify snapshot is created on cancellation request status change
- Test cancelled item restores stock via inventory record
- Test remaining items in order continue processing normally
- Test order status becomes "cancelled" when all items cancelled

### Refund Requests
- Test request refund for order item with status "delivered"
- Test cannot request refund for item with status other than "delivered"
- Test refund request includes reason (text)
- Test refund can be requested within 7 days of delivery
- Test refund request after 7 days should fail
- Test seller can approve refund request
- Test seller can reject refund request
- Verify snapshot is created on refund request status change
- Test refunded item restores stock via inventory record
- Test remaining items in order are unaffected
- Test order status becomes "refunded" when all items refunded

## Reviews & Ratings Tests

### Review Management
- Test create review for delivered product (rating 1-5, optional text)
- Test review can only be written after item status is "delivered"
- Test one review per product per order
- Test edit own review
- Verify review snapshot is created on edit
- Test delete own review (snapshot preserved)
- Test view product reviews (sorted by newest)
- Test average rating calculated from non-deleted reviews only
- Test average rating displayed on product listing and detail page
- Test review count displayed on product listing and detail page

## Seller Dashboard Tests
- Test seller view shop summary (total products, total order items, pending cancellation requests, pending refund requests)
- Test seller view list of order items for their products
- Test seller can filter order items by status

## Administrator Tests

### Admin Request Management
- Test any user can submit request to become administrator (with reason)
- Test super administrator can view pending admin requests
- Test super administrator can approve admin requests
- Test super administrator can reject admin requests
- Test approved user becomes regular administrator

### Seller Management
- Test administrator view pending seller approvals
- Test administrator approve seller registration
- Test administrator reject seller registration (with reason)
- Test rejected seller can submit new registration request
- Test administrator suspend seller account
- Test suspended seller products hidden from search and listings
- Test suspended seller products cannot be purchased
- Test suspended seller can still process existing orders
- Test suspended seller cannot create new products
- Test suspended seller cannot edit existing products
- Test administrator unsuspend seller account (products become visible)
- Test administrator ban seller account (cannot log in, existing orders remain)
- Test administrator unban seller account

### Category Management

### Product Oversight
- Test administrator view all products on platform

### Order Oversight
- Test administrator view all orders on platform

- Test administrator force-refund entire order

## Snapshot Validation Tests
- Test product snapshot created on product edit

- Test seller profile snapshot created on profile edit

- Test cancellation request snapshot created on status change

- Test order item snapshot saved with order (product, variant, seller profile at time of purchase)

## Integration Tests
- Test complete customer journey: register → browse products → add to cart → checkout → place order → track shipment → confirm delivery → write review
- Test complete seller journey: register → wait for approval → create product → add variants → manage inventory → receive order → create shipment → approve/reject cancellation/refund
- Test complete admin journey: approve seller → approve category → view products → oversee orders → manage users
- Test order with multiple items from different sellers creates separate shipments
- Test order with multiple items from same seller can be bundled into single shipment
- Test cancellation of one item in multi-item order affects only that item
- Test refund of one item in multi-item order affects only that item
- Test inventory correctly tracks stock changes across multiple orders
- Test average rating updates correctly when reviews are added/edited/deleted

Test that an administrator can successfully retrieve detailed profile information for any customer account on the platform. This is the primary success path for administrative customer oversight.

   - id: UUID format
   - email: customer's authentication email
   - display_name: customer's optional display name (can be null)
   - phone_number: customer's optional phone number (can be null)
   - account_status: one of 'active', 'suspended', or 'banned'
   - created_at: account creation timestamp in ISO 8601 format
   - updated_at: last modification timestamp in ISO 8601 format
   - deleted_at: null (customer is not soft-deleted)
4. Verify password_hash is NOT included in the response (security requirement)
5. Verify HTTP status code is 200 OK

Business Rules Validated:
- Administrators have full visibility into all customer accounts for oversight purposes
- Customer profile data is accessible regardless of account status (active, suspended, banned)
- Sensitive authentication credentials (password_hash) are never exposed in API responses
- Soft-deleted customers (deleted_at is not null) should return 404 Not Found

4. Customer calls with href filter (partial match)

Validation Points:
- Status filtering correctly computes active/expired based on expired_at timestamp
- IP filter uses exact match only
- Href and referrer filters support partial matching (LIKE)
- Multiple filters can be combined in single request
- Pagination respects all applied filters

Business Logic:
- Status is computed at query time, not stored as explicit column
- Connection metadata filtering helps customers identify suspicious sessions
- Customers can identify and terminate sessions from unrecognized devices

scenario.draft:
Verify that customers can only access their own sessions and cannot view other users' session data (security isolation).

Scenario 1: Customer Can View Own Sessions
1. Customer A joins platform
2. Customer A logs in from multiple devices (creates 3 sessions)
3. Customer A calls PATCH /ecommerceMall/customer/sessions
4. System returns exactly 3 sessions belonging to Customer A
5. All session data is complete and accurate

Scenario 2: Customer Cannot View Other Customer's Sessions
1. Customer A and Customer B both join platform
2. Customer A logs in (creates session)
3. Customer B logs in (creates session)
4. Customer A calls PATCH /ecommerceMall/customer/sessions
5. System returns ONLY Customer A's sessions (Customer B's sessions excluded)
6. Response contains no indication that other sessions exist

Scenario 3: Customer Cannot Access Session by ID Manipulation
1. Customer A obtains session ID from their own session list
2. Customer A attempts to query specific session via GET /ecommerceMall/customer/sessions/{sessionId}
3. System validates session ownership before returning data
4. If Customer A tries to access Customer B's session ID, system returns 404 or 403

Validation Points:
- Session queries are filtered by authenticated customer ID from JWT token
- No session data from other customers appears in response
- Ownership validation occurs at database query level
- Error responses do not leak information about other users' sessions

Business Logic:
- Strict data isolation enforced by authorization middleware
- JWT token contains customer ID used for ownership validation
- Database queries include WHERE clause filtering by customer ID
- Security policy prevents cross-user data access

Security Considerations:
- Sensitive token information never exposed in any response
- Session metadata (ip, href, referrer) is safe for customer viewing
- Customers can identify unauthorized access by reviewing session list
- Customers can terminate suspicious sessions via DELETE endpoint

scenario.draft:
Test that anyone can successfully retrieve a paginated list of images for a product. The scenario validates:

1. **Primary Success Path**: Retrieve all images for a product with default pagination parameters. The response should include:
   - Pagination metadata (current page, limit, total records, total pages)
   - Array of image summaries with id, url, sort_order, is_primary, and created_at fields
   - Images sorted by sort_order ascending
   - The first image (sort_order=0) should have is_primary=true

2. **Pagination Validation**: Test with different page and limit values to verify pagination metadata is calculated correctly. Verify that records count matches the actual number of images returned.

3. **Image Summary Fields**: Validate that each image summary contains all required fields (id, url, sort_order, is_primary, created_at) with correct data types and formats.

4. **Sort Order Verification**: Confirm images are returned in ascending sort_order order, with the thumbnail image (sort_order=0) appearing first.

5. **Public Access**: Verify the endpoint is accessible without authentication - anyone can retrieve product images.

functions.name: test_api_product_image_retrieval_by_seller

scenario.draft:
Test that sellers can filter product images by primary/thumbnail status using the is_primary query parameter. The scenario validates:

1. **Filter by Primary Images Only**: Set is_primary=true in the request body. Verify that only images with is_primary=true (typically the thumbnail with sort_order=0) are returned in the results.

2. **Filter by Non-Primary Images**: Set is_primary=false in the request body. Verify that only images with is_primary=false are returned, excluding the thumbnail image.

3. **No Filter (All Images)**: Set is_primary=null or omit the parameter. Verify that all images for the product are returned regardless of primary status.

4. **Pagination with Filtering**: Test that pagination metadata correctly reflects the filtered result set. When filtering by is_primary=true, the records count should match the number of primary images (typically 1).

5. **Sort Order Preservation**: Verify that filtering does not affect the sort_order ordering - filtered results should still be sorted by sort_order ascending.

6. **Edge Case - Only Primary Image**: Test with a product that has only one image (the thumbnail). Verify that is_primary=false filter returns empty results with correct pagination metadata (records=0, pages=0).

functions.name: test_api_product_image_filtering_by_primary_status

scenario.draft:
Test that sellers can paginate through product images and filter by sort order range using sort_order_min and sort_order_max parameters. The scenario validates:

1. **Basic Pagination**: Test with page=1, limit=10 to retrieve the first page of images. Verify pagination metadata shows current=1, limit=10, and correct records/pages counts.

2. **Sort Order Range Filtering**: Set sort_order_min and sort_order_max to retrieve only images within a specific range. For example, sort_order_min=2, sort_order_max=5 should return only images with sort_order values between 2 and 5 (inclusive).

3. **Combined Filtering**: Test combining is_primary filter with sort_order range. Verify that both filters are applied correctly and the result set reflects the intersection of both conditions.

4. **Pagination Across Multiple Pages**: Create a product with many images (more than the page limit). Test retrieving page 1, page 2, etc., and verify that each page returns the correct subset of images without duplicates or gaps.

5. **Empty Result Set**: Test with a sort_order range that doesn't match any images (e.g., sort_order_min=100, sort_order_max=200 for a product with only 5 images). Verify that the response returns an empty data array with pagination metadata showing records=0, pages=0.

6. **Boundary Values**: Test with sort_order_min=0 (the thumbnail) and sort_order_max set to the highest sort_order value. Verify that all images are included in the result.

scenario.draft:
Test that an administrator can successfully retrieve a category snapshot after a category has been modified. This validates the primary success path for the category snapshot retrieval endpoint.

Test Steps:
1. Authenticate as an administrator via /ecommerceMall/auth/admin/join
2. Create a category via /ecommerceMall/admin/categories
3. Update the category name and description via /ecommerceMall/admin/categories/{categoryId}
4. Retrieve the list of snapshots for the category via PATCH /ecommerceMall/admin/category-snapshots to get the snapshot ID
5. Retrieve the specific snapshot via GET /ecommerceMall/admin/category-snapshots/{snapshotId}

Validation Points:
- Snapshot response contains correct id, category_id, admin_id
- previous_values contains the category state before modification (original name, description, parentId)
- current_values contains the category state after modification (updated name, description, parentId)
- category object contains correct category details (id, name, parent, created_at, deleted_at)
- admin object contains correct administrator details (id, email, admin_grade, account_status, created_at)
- created_at timestamp reflects when the snapshot was created
- JSON fields (previous_values, current_values) are properly parsed as objects

Business Logic Validated:
- Category modifications trigger snapshot creation
- Snapshots preserve complete before/after state
- Administrators can access all category snapshots
- Snapshot data structure matches IEcommerceMallCategorySnapshot schema

5. The snapshot is immutable and cannot be modified or deleted
6. The authorization check passes because the order belongs to the authenticated customer

11. Verify pagination metadata includes: current page, limit, total records, total pages

**Expected Results**:
- Cart items are correctly filtered and sorted
- Subtotals are calculated as quantity × current variant price (or base price if variant price is null)
- Cart total excludes unavailable items
- Pagination metadata is accurate
- Customer can only see their own cart items (data isolation)

scenario.draft:
Test that cart items reflect current product prices after price changes, ensuring customers see accurate pricing at checkout.

**Setup**: Customer joins, seller creates product with variants at specific prices, customer adds variants to cart, seller updates prices.

**Test Steps**:
1. Customer joins and seller creates product with base price of $100
2. Seller creates variant with price override of $120
3. Customer adds variant to cart with quantity 2
4. Customer views cart - verify subtotal is $240 (2 × $120 variant price)
5. Seller updates variant price to $150
6. Customer views cart again - verify subtotal is now $300 (2 × $150 current variant price)
7. Verify cart item displays current price ($150), not the price at time of addition ($120)
8. Seller removes variant price override (sets to null)
9. Customer views cart - verify subtotal is now $200 (2 × $100 base price)
10. Seller updates base product price to $90
11. Customer views cart - verify subtotal is now $180 (2 × $90 updated base price)
12. Seller deletes the variant entirely
13. Customer views cart - verify variant is marked as is_available=false
14. Verify cart total updates correctly after each price change
15. Verify pagination and filtering work correctly with price-sorted results

**Expected Results**:
- Cart items always display current prices, not historical prices at time of addition
- Subtotals are recalculated immediately when prices change
- Cart total reflects all price updates
- Variant price override takes precedence over base price
- When variant price is null, base price is used
- Deleted variants are marked as unavailable
- Price sorting works correctly (low-to-high and high-to-low)

Test that deleted products are automatically removed from customer wishlists and cannot be retrieved.

**Setup Steps:**
1. Create a customer account via POST /ecommerceMall/auth/customer/join
2. Create a seller account via POST /ecommerceMall/auth/seller/join

- Response status code is 404 Not Found
- Error message indicates the wishlist entry or product has been deleted
- The wishlist entry is automatically removed when product is deleted (cascade behavior)
- This happens within the same transaction to prevent orphaned references
- No notification is sent to the customer about the auto-removal

**Business Rule Verification:**
- Deleted products SHALL be automatically removed from all customer wishlists (section 790)
- Product deletion cascades to wishlists atomically to prevent orphaned references
- Wishlist entry is hidden from customer view but may be preserved for analytics (deleted_at populated, active=false)
- The operation respects soft-delete semantics where deleted_at marks removal from visible wishlist

scenario.draft: Test that cancellation requests are blocked for order items that have been shipped. A customer places an order, then the seller ships the order item (changing status from 'paid' to 'shipped'). When the customer attempts to submit a cancellation request for this shipped item, the system must reject the request with an appropriate error. The test validates the business rule that cancellation is only allowed for items with 'paid' status (pre-shipment). After order placement, the seller creates a shipment for the order item, transitioning its status to 'shipped'. The customer then attempts to create a cancellation request, which should fail because the item is no longer in 'paid' status. The system should provide a clear error message explaining that cancellation is not available for shipped items and that refund requests are available instead after delivery.

**Primary Success Path**:
1. Customer authenticates via join
2. Seller authenticates via join
3. Admin creates category
4. Seller creates product and variant
5. Customer adds variant to cart
6. Customer creates shipping address
7. Customer places order (creates order item)
8. Seller creates shipment to change item status to 'shipped'
9. Customer confirms delivery to change item status to 'delivered'
10. Customer creates refund request (within 7-day window)
11. Seller retrieves the refund request by orderItemId and requestId
12. Verify response contains: id, orderItem reference with product details, reason, status='pending', requested_at, responded_at=null, days_since_delivery, created_at, updated_at

**Business Validations**:
- Seller can view refund requests for their own products
- Refund request details are complete and accurate
- Seller can see customer's refund reason
- Status shows current workflow state
- days_since_delivery is available for seller review

**Edge Cases**:
- Seller cannot access refund requests for products from other sellers (403)
- Accessing non-existent request returns 404
- Soft-deleted refund requests are not accessible (404)

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_already_responded_conflict

scenario.draft:
Test administrator force-approves a refund request, bypassing the standard 7-day refund window restriction. This scenario validates the admin override capability for policy enforcement.

**Setup Phase**:
1. Create admin account via POST /ecommerceMall/auth/admin/join
2. Create seller account via POST /ecommerceMall/auth/seller/join
3. Create customer account via POST /ecommerceMall/auth/customer/join
4. Create category via POST /ecommerceMall/admin/categories (admin)
5. Create product via POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products (seller)
6. Create product variant via POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants (seller)
7. Create shipping address via POST /ecommerceMall/customer/addresses (customer)
8. Add variant to cart via POST /ecommerceMall/customer/cart-items (customer)
9. Create order via POST /ecommerceMall/customer/orders (customer) - order item status becomes 'paid'
10. Simulate shipment and delivery - order item status becomes 'delivered'
11. Wait 8+ days past delivery date to exceed 7-day refund window
12. Create refund request via POST /ecommerceMall/customer/order-items/{orderItemId}/refund-requests (customer) - request status is 'pending'

**Test Phase**:
13. Admin updates refund request via PUT /ecommerceMall/admin/order-items/{orderItemId}/refund-requests/{requestId} with status='approved'

**Validation Points**:
- Refund request status changes from 'pending' to 'approved'
- responded_at timestamp is set to current time
- Order item status changes from 'delivered' to 'refunded'
- Inventory record is created with positive quantityChange equal to order item quantity, reason='refund_approved'
- Parent order status is recalculated (if all items refunded, order status becomes 'refunded')
- Refund request snapshot is created capturing previous and current values
- The 7-day window restriction is bypassed for admin force-approval
- Transaction is atomic - all updates succeed or all rollback together

functions.name: test_api_admin_force_approve_refund_request

scenario.draft:
Test administrator rejects a refund request, preventing the refund from being processed. This scenario validates the admin rejection workflow and ensures order item status remains unchanged.

**Setup Phase**:
1. Create admin account via POST /ecommerceMall/auth/admin/join
2. Create seller account via POST /ecommerceMall/auth/seller/join
3. Create customer account via POST /ecommerceMall/auth/customer/join
4. Create category via POST /ecommerceMall/admin/categories (admin)
5. Create product via POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products (seller)
6. Create product variant via POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants (seller)
7. Create shipping address via POST /ecommerceMall/customer/addresses (customer)
8. Add variant to cart via POST /ecommerceMall/customer/cart-items (customer)
9. Create order via POST /ecommerceMall/customer/orders (customer) - order item status becomes 'paid'
10. Create shipment via POST /ecommerceMall/seller/shipments (seller) - order item status becomes 'shipped'
11. Confirm delivery via POST /ecommerceMall/customer/shipments/{shipmentId}/confirm-delivery (customer) - order item status becomes 'delivered'
12. Create refund request via POST /ecommerceMall/customer/order-items/{orderItemId}/refund-requests (customer) - request status is 'pending', within 7-day window

**Test Phase**:
13. Admin updates refund request via PUT /ecommerceMall/admin/order-items/{orderItemId}/refund-requests/{requestId} with status='rejected' and rejection reason

**Validation Points**:
- Refund request status changes from 'pending' to 'rejected'
- responded_at timestamp is set to current time
- Order item status remains 'delivered' (unchanged)
- No inventory record is created (stock not restored)
- Refund request snapshot is created capturing previous and current values
- Parent order status remains unchanged (not 'refunded')
- Customer can submit a new refund request only if still within 7-day window and previous request was rejected
- Transaction is atomic - all updates succeed or all rollback together

scenario.draft:
Test the administrator force-cancel workflow for order management oversight. An administrator should be able to force-cancel an order that is in 'paid' or 'shipped' status, which triggers automatic inventory restoration and audit snapshot creation for all order items.

Test Steps:
1. Administrator joins the system via /auth/admin/join
2. Administrator creates a category via /admin/categories (required for product creation)
3. Seller joins the system via /auth/seller/join
4. Seller creates a product via /seller/products referencing the category
5. Seller creates a product variant via /seller/products/{productId}/variants with stock quantity
6. Customer joins the system via /auth/customer/join
7. Customer creates a shipping address via /customer/addresses
8. Customer adds the variant to cart via /customer/cart-items
9. Customer places an order via /customer/orders (order status becomes 'paid')
10. Administrator force-cancels the order by updating status to 'cancelled' via PUT /admin/orders/{orderId}

Validation Points:
- Verify the order status changes from 'paid' to 'cancelled'
- Verify inventory records are created for each order item with positive quantityChange equal to item quantity
- Verify the inventory record reason is 'admin_force_cancel'
- Verify order item snapshots are created capturing the before/after state with changedBy=admin_id
- Verify all order items in the order are updated to 'cancelled' status
- Verify the order.updated_at timestamp is updated
- Verify the response returns the complete updated order object with new status

Business Logic:
- Force-cancellation should work on any order regardless of customer or seller ownership
- Inventory restoration must be atomic with order status update (transaction rollback on failure)
- Snapshots must be created for audit trail compliance
- Multi-seller orders should have all items cancelled uniformly

scenario.draft:
Test the administrator force-refund workflow for order management oversight. An administrator should be able to force-refund an order that is in 'delivered' status (or any status via admin override), which processes refunds, restores inventory, and creates audit snapshots.

Test Steps:
1. Administrator joins the system via /auth/admin/join
2. Administrator creates a category via /admin/categories
3. Seller joins the system via /auth/seller/join
4. Seller creates a product via /seller/products
5. Seller creates a product variant via /seller/products/{productId}/variants
6. Customer joins the system via /auth/customer/join
7. Customer creates a shipping address via /customer/addresses
8. Customer adds variant to cart via /customer/cart-items
9. Customer places order via /customer/orders (order status becomes 'paid')
10. (Simulate shipping) Order items transition to 'shipped' status
11. (Simulate delivery) Order items transition to 'delivered' status
12. Administrator force-refunds the order by updating status to 'refunded' via PUT /admin/orders/{orderId}

Validation Points:
- Verify the order status changes to 'refunded'
- Verify inventory records are created for each order item with positive quantityChange
- Verify the inventory record reason is 'admin_force_refund'
- Verify order item snapshots are created with changedBy=admin_id
- Verify all order items are updated to 'refunded' status
- Verify the order.updated_at timestamp reflects the admin action
- Verify the response includes complete updated order with all fields

Business Logic:
- Force-refund can be applied to orders in any status (admin override capability)
- Refund processing must restore stock quantities via inventory records
- Snapshots must capture complete before/after state for dispute resolution
- Transaction must be atomic - rollback on any failure (inventory or snapshot creation)
- Multi-seller orders process all items uniformly regardless of seller ownership

The test should verify that the system returns a paginated list of product summaries including product id, name, base price, main image URL, seller shop name, average rating, and review count. Products should be filtered by the provided category ID and include products from all subcategories under that category. The response should include pagination metadata with current page, limit, total records, and total pages. Products should be sorted by default (newest first) and the system should only return active products (status='active') that are not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). The test should validate that the endpoint works without authentication (public access) and that the category ID parameter is properly validated as a UUID format.

functions.name: test_api_category_product_browsing

scenario.draft: Test that when browsing a parent category, the system includes products from all subcategories nested under that category. The test should create a category hierarchy with a parent category and at least one subcategory, then add products to both the parent and subcategory. When querying the parent category endpoint, the response should include products from both the parent category and all its subcategories. This validates the category hierarchy traversal logic where the system queries products where category_id matches the provided categoryId OR any subcategory's parent_id chain. The test should verify that products are correctly associated with their categories and that the hierarchical relationship is properly maintained in the database queries.

functions.name: test_api_category_product_includes_subcategories

scenario.draft: Test that when browsing a category with no products assigned, the system returns a valid response with an empty data array and correct pagination metadata. The test should create a category without any products, then query the category products endpoint. The response should have pagination.current set to 1, pagination.limit set to the requested or default limit (20), pagination.records set to 0, and pagination.pages set to 0. The data array should be empty. This validates that the system handles empty categories gracefully and returns consistent pagination metadata even when there are no products. The category itself should still be visible in the category listing (as per category browsing requirements) but the product listing should show zero results.

functions.name: test_api_category_empty_product_listing

scenario.draft: Test that administrators can retrieve category analytics data with various filtering options. The test should verify that the endpoint returns paginated category summaries with computed product counts (total_product_count and active_product_count). Validate that search filters work correctly on category name and description fields. Test parent_category_id filtering to retrieve only subcategories of a specific parent. Verify date range filtering with created_at_from and created_at_to parameters. Confirm cursor-based pagination returns correct pagination metadata (current, limit, records, pages). Ensure deleted categories are excluded by default from results.

Compare results between include_deleted=true and include_deleted=false (default) to confirm deleted categories are filtered out by default. Validate that deleted categories show accurate product counts even after deletion, preserving historical analytics data for audit purposes.

instruction:
# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform Business Logic Implementation Requirements

## Authentication Business Logic

### Customer Authentication
- Implement customer registration with email validation and password hashing
- Implement customer login with credential verification and JWT token generation
- Implement password change requiring current password verification
- Implement account deletion with cascade handling (preserve orders, mark reviews as "deleted user")

### Seller Authentication
- Implement seller registration with email validation and password hashing
- Implement seller login with credential verification and JWT token generation
- Implement password change requiring current password verification
- Implement account deletion with validation:
  - Check for pending orders (paid or shipped status)
  - Check for pending cancellation or refund requests
  - Delete products from listings
  - Preserve order history and snapshots
  - Preserve shop name in past orders

### Administrator Authentication
- Implement administrator login
- Implement admin request submission with reason
- Implement admin approval/rejection workflow (super admin only)
- Implement grade promotion/demotion with self-protection (super admin cannot demote themselves)

## Customer Profile Business Logic
- Implement profile retrieval (display name, phone number)
- Implement profile update with snapshot creation
- Ensure snapshots record: timestamp, changed fields, before/after values

## Address Management Business Logic
- Implement address CRUD operations
- Implement default address setting (only one default per customer)
- Ensure address can be used in orders before deletion

## Category Business Logic
- Implement category listing with subcategory hierarchy (one level nesting)
- Implement category browsing with product listing
- (Admin only) Implement category creation, editing, deletion
- Handle product uncategorization when category deleted

## Product Business Logic

### Product CRUD
- Implement product creation with required fields validation (name, description, category, base price)
- Implement product retrieval with all related data (images, variants, seller info, reviews)
- Implement product update with snapshot creation for all fields including images
- Implement product deletion with validation:
  - Check for pending order items (paid or shipped status) for any variant
  - Check for pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant
  - Delete all variants and inventory records
  - Preserve snapshots even after deletion

### Product Images
- Implement image upload with multiple images support
- Implement image reordering (first image = thumbnail)
- Implement image deletion
- Include image changes in product snapshots

### Product Variants (SKU)
- Implement variant creation with unique SKU code validation
- Implement variant update with snapshot creation
- Implement variant deletion with validation:
  - Check for pending order items (paid or shipped status)
  - Check for pending cancellation or refund requests
- Ensure product must have at least one variant to be purchasable
- Handle products with no variants as "unavailable"

### Product Search
- Implement product search by name with pagination
- Implement category filtering
- Implement price range filtering (min, max)
- Implement in-stock filtering
- Implement sorting: newest, price low-to-high, price high-to-low
- Search across all sellers

### Product Listing
- Implement product listing with: main image, name, base price/price range, seller shop name, average rating
- Implement pagination

## Inventory Management Business Logic
- Implement inventory history tracking (not snapshots)
- Implement inventory record creation: quantity change, reason, timestamp
- Calculate current stock by summing all inventory records
- Implement restock (positive quantity change)
- Implement adjustment/loss (negative quantity change)
- Auto-create negative inventory record on order placement
- Auto-create positive inventory record on cancellation/refund
- Mark variant as "out of stock" when stock reaches 0
- Prevent out of stock variants from being added to cart

## Wishlist Business Logic
- Implement add product to wishlist (product level, not variant)
- Implement wishlist retrieval with pagination
- Implement remove product from wishlist
- Auto-remove deleted products from all wishlists

## Shopping Cart Business Logic
- Implement add variant to cart with quantity
- Combine quantities for same variant (not separate line items)
- Implement cart retrieval with: product name, variant options, price, quantity, subtotal, total
- Implement quantity update
- Implement item removal
- Show stock availability warning when cart quantity exceeds available stock
- Mark deleted or out of stock variants as unavailable in cart

## Checkout & Order Business Logic

### Checkout
- Implement checkout from cart
- Validate unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Implement shipping address selection (or use default)
- Implement order summary review (items, prices, address, total)
- Implement order placement with payment confirmation
- Handle payment failure (no order created, customer can retry)
- Handle payment success (order created)
- Prevent shipping address changes after order placed

### Order Management
- Implement order history retrieval (paginated, newest first)
- Implement order detail retrieval (items, shipping address, shipments)
- Calculate order status from item statuses

### Order Item Status Logic
- Implement independent order item status tracking: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded

### Order Status Logic
- Implement order status derivation:
  - All items paid → "paid"
  - Any item shipped (none delivered) → "shipped"
  - All items delivered → "delivered"
  - All items cancelled → "cancelled"
  - All items refunded → "refunded"
  - Mixed states → "partially completed"

## Shipping & Tracking Business Logic

### Shipment Management
- Implement seller view of order items needing shipping
- Implement shipment creation:
  - Select one or more items from same seller
  - Enter tracking information (carrier name, tracking number)
  - All items in shipment share tracking info
  - Change items to "shipped" status
- Ensure different sellers create separate shipments

### Delivery Confirmation
- Implement customer view of shipments
- Implement delivery confirmation per shipment
- Change all items in confirmed shipment to "delivered" status
- Implement auto-delivery after 14 days from shipping

## Cancellation & Refund Business Logic

### Cancellation Requests
- Implement cancellation request for order item with status "paid" (not shipped)
- Include reason (text) in request
- Implement seller approve/reject cancellation request
- Create snapshot on status change
- On approval: cancel item, process refund, restore stock via inventory record
- Remaining items continue processing normally
- Update order status to "cancelled" when all items cancelled

### Refund Requests
- Implement refund request for order item with status "delivered"
- Include reason (text) in request
- Enforce 7-day refund window from delivery date
- Implement seller approve/reject refund request
- Create snapshot on status change
- On approval: refund item, restore stock via inventory record
- Remaining items unaffected
- Update order status to "refunded" when all items refunded

## Reviews & Ratings Business Logic

### Review Management
- Implement review creation for delivered products
- Enforce: one review per product per order
- Include rating (1-5 stars, required) and optional text
- Implement review edit with snapshot creation
- Implement review delete (snapshot preserved)
- Implement review retrieval sorted by newest
- Calculate average rating from non-deleted reviews only
- Display average rating and review count on product listing and detail page

## Seller Dashboard Business Logic
- Implement shop summary: total products, total order items, pending cancellation requests, pending refund requests
- Implement order item list for seller's products
- Implement filtering by status

## Administrator Business Logic

### Admin Request Management
- Implement admin request submission with reason
- Implement pending admin requests view (super admin only)
- Implement approve/reject admin requests (super admin only)
- On approval: user becomes regular administrator

### Seller Management
- Implement pending seller approvals view
- Implement approve/reject seller registrations (with reason for rejection)
- Implement seller suspension:
  - Hide products from search and listings
  - Prevent product purchase
  - Allow existing order processing (ship, respond to cancellation/refund)
  - Prevent new product creation
  - Prevent product editing
- Implement seller unsuspension (products become visible)
- Implement seller ban/unban (banned cannot log in, existing orders remain)

### Category Management
- Implement category/subcategory creation
- Implement category name and description editing
- Implement category deletion (products become uncategorized)

### Product Oversight
- Implement all products view
- Implement product snapshot view (any product)
- Implement product deletion (policy violations)
- Preserve snapshots after deletion

### Order Oversight
- Implement all orders view
- Implement force-cancel individual items or entire orders (refund customer, restore stock)
- Implement force-refund individual items or entire orders

### User Management
- Implement all customer accounts view
- Implement customer ban/unban (banned cannot log in)
- Implement all seller accounts view

## Snapshot Business Logic
- Implement snapshot creation on all data modifications:
  - Products (all fields including images)
  - Product variants (SKU code, option values, price)
  - Seller profiles (shop name, description, logo)
  - Order items (product, variant, seller profile at purchase time)
  - Reviews (rating, text content)
  - Cancellation requests (reason, status changes)
  - Refund requests (reason, status changes)
- Product snapshots include all variants at that moment (product-snapshot → product-snapshot-SKU)
- Ensure snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Implement snapshot retrieval for relevant parties (owners, administrators)
- Preserve snapshots even after entity deletion

## Security & Validation
- Implement JWT authentication for all protected routes
- Implement role-based access control (customer, seller, admin, super admin)
- Implement input validation for all endpoints
- Implement business rule validation before state changes
- Implement audit logging for all sensitive operations

## Error Handling
- Implement proper HTTP status codes
- Implement meaningful error messages
- Implement transaction rollback on failures
- Implement proper error responses for validation failures
